record.title: Partially temporal coherent spatiotemporal Laguerre-Gaussian and its propagation dynamics
record.abstract: Optical spatiotemporal vortices carrying transverse photonic orbital angular momentum have become an intense research topic in the recent study of structured light fields. Despite being mainly studied within the framework of fully coherent optical pulses, the complex topologies of the light field are also investigated with partially coherent light sources, offering an alternative pathway in applications. In this work, we theoretically and experimentally investigate partially temporally coherent spatiotemporal Laguerre-Gaussian (STLG) field with independently controllable radial and azimuthal indices. The spatiotemporal topological information, carried by the structured amplified spontaneous emission source, are well preserved in the presence of inherent instantaneous random temporal phase fluctuations. Under combined spatiotemporal astigmatism and group velocity dispersion, the partially temporally coherent STLG field can be converted into spatiotemporal Hermite-Gaussian (STHG) field. Both structures maintain their spatiotemporal characteristics after propagating through scattering media. Partially temporally coherent structured light fields may offer new insights into photonic topology and complex wave dynamics, with potential applications in high-fidelity optical communications and high-dimensional information processing in highly scattering environments.

record.title: Electromagnetic emission at the Langmuir frequency from laser interaction with an unmagnetized plasma
record.abstract: We present the first experimental observation of electromagnetic emission at the Langmuir frequency, $ω_p$, resulting from laser-plasma interaction in an underdense and unmagnetised plasma. The emission is spatially resolved and analyzed in polarization. It originates from an electrostatic wave excited by the Raman instability. Despite its frequency being very close to the plasma's cutoff frequency, $ω_{pe}$, this radiation can escape the plasma by following the decreasing slope of the plasma density profile. Radiation at $2ω_p$, is also observed. This experimental platform offers a powerful tool to explore the processes of wave coupling at the origin of some radio solar bursts.

record.title: Implicit Bias of (Stochastic) Gradient Descent on Deep Linear Diagonal Networks
record.abstract: Modern machine learning models are often overparameterized, i.e., have more parameters than training data. This typically implies that the loss function admits multiple minimizers so that training methods (and their hyperparameter choices) have significant influence on the computed solution. We study this so-called implicit bias phenomenon in the context of training deep linear diagonal networks. Previous work has shown that the gradient flow for learning such networks converges to (almost) sparse solutions when initialized small. For an arbitrary number of layers, we extend this analysis to the practically more realistic (stochastic) gradient descent iterations. Our approach identifies (stochastic) gradient descent as a perturbed (stochastic) mirror gradient descent. This allows us to establish convergence and characterize the limiting solution, relating it to weighted $\ell_1$-minimization. Moreover, we provide sufficient conditions on the step sizes and quantify the influence of the step sizes on the implicit bias.

record.title: Inverse-IMPRESSION: A Graph-Based Platform for Molecular Structure Elucidation from Experimental NMR Spectroscopic Properties
record.publication: Journal of the American Chemical Society
record.abstract: Abstract Here, we present a platform built on our inverted graph transformer network, IMPRESSION-G2, which can accurately and rapidly reconstruct molecular bonding directly from experimental nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic information. It comprises three interconnected stages: a one-shot model that reads in NMR parameters and uses these to predict bond connectivity between atoms; a structure correction stage that corrects the predicted structures by removing uncertain bonds and iteratively reassigning them; and noise-augmented multishot prediction, generating an ensemble of candidate structures, which are ranked to identify the best-fit structure. By integrating a range of 1H and 13C NMR data, including two-dimensional (2D) experiments such as COSY, HSQC, and HMBC, the inverse-IMPRESSION platform correctly identifies the structures of 77.8% of molecules with up to 30 heavy atoms (H, C, N, O, and F) using simulated NMR data, and 11 of 19 (58%) molecules using experimental NMR data. The experimental structures solved are representative of the complex structures in synthetic and natural products that routinely challenge chemists, assessed by high nSPS scores (greater than 40) for successfully elucidated structures and molecular weights of up to 480 Da. The inverse-IMPRESSION framework thus provides a highly effective approach for automated molecular structure elucidation by using graph-based machine learning on experimental data.

record.title: Variational quantum thermalization of environment-coupled DNA sequence biases
record.abstract: Abstract Understanding whether environmental conditions bias the statistical weight of specific genomic configurations requires a framework connecting molecular interactions, thermal fluctuations, and sequence-level observables. Here, we model DNA as an open quantum system coupled to an environmental thermal bath (represented as an external bosonic field) and parameterize the underlying molecular interaction energies (effective Hamiltonian terms) directly from prescribed nucleotide sequences. To evaluate sequence distributions at thermodynamic equilibrium, we compare two finite-temperature strategies at fixed inverse temperature ( β = 1): classical Bayesian optimization targeting the exact thermodynamic equilibrium distribution (the Gibbs state), and quantum simulation using a Variational Quantum Thermalizer (VQT) implemented via a nine-layer parameterized quantum circuit. Both methods optimize the same interaction energy model and target-sequence objective across short oligomers ( N = 2–5 base pairs), using 200 outer evaluations. Benchmarking against a uniform sequence distribution, exact-Gibbs optimization enhances target-sequence probabilities by factors of 9.11, 25.64, 54.51, and 159.87. The VQT approach similarly yields substantial target enrichment across all sequence lengths, achieving enhancement factors between 9.85 and 62.77. By evaluating the VQT-selected Hamiltonians against exact Gibbs calculations, we decouple optimization errors in parameter learning from approximation errors inherent to the variational quantum circuit. While concordance with the exact-Gibbs optimum is high in shorter oligomers, larger systems exhibit heightened sensitivity to variational thermal approximations. These results demonstrate that environment-induced sequence biases can be systematically captured within a variational quantum simulation framework, bridging biophysical models of DNA thermodynamics with quantum algorithms for finite-temperature state preparation. Crucially, the resulting equilibrium probabilities represent intrinsic thermo-dynamic biases rather than realized evolutionary substitution rates, which remain governed by kinetic activation barriers, replication fidelity, and enzymatic DNA repair.

record.title: Next-to-leading-order QCD study of $e^+e^- \to η_c + c\bar{c}$ at $B$ factories
record.abstract: We study the process $e^+e^- \to γ^\ast \to η_c + c\bar{c} + X$ at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD within the framework of nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization, retaining the color-singlet contribution at leading order in the heavy-quark relative velocity $v$. At the $e^+e^-$ collision energy $\sqrt{s} = 10.6~\mathrm{GeV}$, with $m_c = 1.5~\mathrm{GeV}$ and $μ_R = 2m_c$, the direct cross section increases from $58.7~\mathrm{fb}$ at leading order (LO) to $118~\mathrm{fb}$ at NLO, corresponding to a $K$ factor of approximately $2.0$. Including the radiative feed-down contributions of the $J/ψ$ and $h_c(1P)$ states yields an estimated prompt production rate of $131~\mathrm{fb}$. The NLO corrections substantially enhance both the angular and momentum distributions, while the momentum spectrum retains a similar overall profile. These results establish an NLO color-singlet baseline for $η_c$ production associated with open charm at Belle II, complementary to studies of charmonium production in hadronic collisions.

record.title: Inkitiate: Initiating and Steering Agent Assistance through Ink in a Spatial Workspace
record.abstract: Handwriting and sketching help people develop ideas around information. As this work unfolds, users may seek assistance with finding, understanding, and organizing materials. We investigate how ink can initiate and steer agent assistance in this process. An eight-participant formative study explored desired assistance and interaction expectations, informing three connected activities: bringing materials in, thinking with materials, and shaping the space. We present Inkitiate, a spatial workspace for ink-based agent assistance in knowledge work. Through ink, users retrieve external materials, build on accumulated content and results, and reorganize the canvas, while inspecting and guiding agent actions. In a study with eighteen participants, users reported favorable usability and low perceived workload, and used retained ink and materials to develop further ink queries. An ink-query vocabulary and cases reveal how users combine linguistic and graphical expressions to direct agents. These findings inform ink-based agent interaction design for expressive requests and continued work with materials.

Solving quantified constraint satisfaction problems with applications to control
record.publication: 29th ACM International Conference on Hybrid Systems: Computation and Control, May 2026, Saint-Malo (35400), France
record.abstract: Many problems in control can be expressed as quantified constraints, such as robust forward and backward reachability, synthesis of controllers, solutions to motion planning problems. In this paper, we develop a method for computing inner and outer approximations of global solutions to very general quantified constraints, generalizing widely the state of the art on similar problems, usually restricted to at most one alternation of quantifiers or to local solutions. By global solutions, we mean characterizing accurately the entire set of solutions, within some prescribed bounds. For this, our approach uses a set inversion technique relying on oracles for set inclusion using local solutions to related quantified reachability problems. We exemplify the approach throughout the paper on different examples related to control problems.

record.title: The Verification Wall in Microbial Metabolomics
record.abstract: Computational methods now propose structures for gut microbial metabolites faster than any laboratory can confirm them. We argue that verification, not generation, is the binding constraint, and that better models will not relieve it. Confirming a structure to the field's own standard means having the molecule in hand. Automation can lower what that costs per compound, but the cost stays proportional to the number of structures and never amortizes across them. Two substitutes are on offer and neither removes that requirement. In-silico spectral prediction ranks candidates instead of confirming one, and the strongest current model puts the right structure first 33.5% of the time on a scaffold-split benchmark. Any assignment resting on spectral similarity is, by the field's own definition, made without a reference standard. Microcrystal diffraction does return a structure, but it needs the compound to crystallize out of a trace mixture, which is a different problem rather than an easier one. We sorted 10,645 computationally inferred metabolite structures by what verifying each would take. Between 5% and 37% have no verification route identified under our analysis. That spread reflects where the thresholds are set rather than a measured count of unverifiable compounds, and the inaccessible ones cluster among the most speculative entries. Those figures understate the problem, because the gut makes far more compounds than any database records. HMDB holds only what someone has already thought worth cataloguing, and structure generators are bounded by nothing at all. The claim is easy to disprove. Show a route that confirms structures as fast as they are proposed. Until someone does, two problems stay unsolved. Nobody knows how to spend a verification budget that will always be too small, or what a biologist may conclude from a structure that was never confirmed.

record.title: Observation of light-induced topological state in graphene
record.abstract: Driving quantum materials with light can reshape not only their electronic band structures but also the geometry of their electronic wavefunctions. In graphene, circularly polarized light is predicted to open gaps at the Dirac points and induce a pseudospin texture and Berry curvature characteristic of the Haldane model, realizing a Floquet Chern insulator. Transport and all-optical measurements have provided evidence for a light-induced anomalous Hall response, but cannot resolve the underlying electronic states in both energy and momentum space. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy has revealed Floquet-Bloch sidebands and hybridization gaps at crossings between Floquet bands. However, these experiments used linearly polarized driving, which preserves time-reversal symmetry and thus does not induce a topological phase. Here, we combine circular-dichroic time-resolved extreme-ultraviolet momentum microscopy with ab initio theory to investigate graphene driven by circularly polarized light. We observe a pump-induced photoemission circular dichroism near the Dirac point that reverses sign with pump helicity and across the Dirac energy, in agreement with our calculations. These results link the measured dichroic response to the light-induced pseudospin texture and its associated Berry curvature, providing spectroscopic evidence for the Floquet-engineered topological insulating state in graphene.

NNLO QCD corrections to direct $J/ψ$ production with open charm at B factories
record.abstract: We calculate the next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD corrections to direct colour-singlet $J/ψ$ production with open charm at B factories, using nested soft-collinear subtraction for massive partons. At $\sqrt{s}=10.6$ GeV, $m_c=1.5$ GeV and $μ_R=2m_c$, we obtain an approximate NNLO cross section of $0.324^{+0.041}_{-0.066}$ pb, with scale uncertainties from $m_c\leqμ_R\leq4m_c$. The total cross section is $18.4\%$ above NLO and exhibits good perturbative convergence through NNLO, with reduced scale dependence. An NLO-based mass extrapolation to $m_c=1.4$ GeV, combined with estimated $ψ(2S)$ feed-down, raises the rate to about $0.59$ pb. The NNLO correction brings the absolute momentum spectrum near its peak closer to Belle's prompt open-charm data, but shifts the angular shape further away from Belle's prompt charm-associated data. The difference in angular shape motivates more precise measurements at Belle II.

record.title: Stability and dispersion analysis of DFDM for the scalar wave equation
record.abstract: Summary This study investigates a particular instantiation of the distributional finite-difference method (DFDM) based on B-splines in the context of solving the 1D scalar wave equation, focusing on two key numerical properties: stability and numerical dispersion. By comparing DFDM against finite-difference and spectral-element methods, we assess the trade-offs between time step restrictions and accuracy. We introduce a cost metric to quantify the computational effort required to achieve a target dispersion error threshold. The results show that, while DFDM has more restrictive stability bounds, it offers superior dispersion performance at lower points per wavelength, making it particularly attractive for applications with tight memory requirements.

Reconciling the Fundamental Plane of Early-Type Galaxies with hydrodynamical simulations: The case of IllustrisTNG100-1
record.publication: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
record.abstract: Abstract The Fundamental Plane (FP) of Early-Type Galaxies (ETGs) encapsulates a tight correlation among their structural and dynamical properties and provides an important benchmark for galaxy formation models. However, cosmological hydrodynamical simulations have historically struggled to reproduce the observed FP tilt, with discrepancies often attributed to flawed feedback physics or insufficient resolution. Using the IllustrisTNG100-1 simulation, we show that adopting observationally motivated measurements, including Sérsic-derived photometric parameters and dynamically inferred velocity dispersions designed to minimise softening-length effects, substantially reduces the discrepancy between simulated and observed FPs. We further explore the impact of non-universal, mass-dependent Initial Mass Function (IMF) variations through forward modelling of their effects on galaxy structural and dynamical quantities. In particular, within the adopted r-band framework, bottom-heavy IMF variations bring the mean FP coefficients into close agreement with observational constraints for both direct and orthogonal fits, while the simulated FP remains thinner than the observed relation. Our results suggest that a significant fraction of the long-standing FP tension arises from how galaxy observables are extracted and interpreted in simulations, although residual discrepancies may still reflect limitations in the underlying baryonic physics. These findings highlight the importance of observational realism and IMF variations for interpreting galaxy scaling relations and for improving the predictive power of hydrodynamical simulations of ETG formation.

record.title: sDMD: Sinkhorn Distribution Matching Distillation
record.abstract: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) distills multi-step diffusion models into few-step generators by minimizing reverse KL divergence. Despite its strong performance, DMD guides samples by local density alone, which introduces two limitations: teacher scores can be unreliable in regions of low teacher density, and the mode-seeking behavior of reverse KL can collapse the student onto a subset of the teacher modes. We first connect DMD to Wasserstein gradient flow, showing that its gradient follows from a fixed-point formulation with integral KL (IKL) as the energy functional. This perspective motivates augmenting IKL with an optimal transport term that addresses these limitations by guiding outlier samples toward the target and promoting mode coverage. We realize this term using Sinkhorn divergence estimated from finite batches. In practice, however, errors in the estimated Sinkhorn velocity can perturb in-domain samples for which IKL guidance is already accurate. To this end, we introduce sDMD, which adaptively activates the Sinkhorn correction based on discriminator outputs, focusing on outlier samples where IKL may be unreliable. With 2--4 sampling steps on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image-20B, and Wan2.1-14B, sDMD outperforms distillation baselines on GenEval, DPG, WISE, and VBench while improving sample diversity over DMD2.

Structure-resolved fold annotation of the medicinal-leech salivary-EV cargo: a Ly-6/uPAR three-finger scaffold and a structurally dark fraction
record.abstract: Abstract Many proteins that medicinal leeches package into salivary extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry no interpretable sequence annotation, so the least-characterised part of a pharmacologically important secretome lacks even a fold assignment. A companion Astral-DIA study of Hirudinaria manillensis 1 nominated 17 ultra-enriched candidate EV cargo proteins. Here we ask whether structure prediction and structural search can assign folds where sequence methods fail, and which candidates remain unresolved under prespecified criteria. With an offline pipeline (ESMFold, TM-align, Foldseek against AFDB-SwissProt and PDB100, UniRef90 search, protein-to-genome alignment), the candidates separate into intracellular/membrane machinery and a secreted, cysteine-dense fraction of three proteins with no Pfam domain. The predicted structure of the leech Protein-sleepless homolog g21166 supports its assignment to the Ly-6/uPAR three-finger fold (TM 0.58 vs CD59; best significant PDB match Lynx1); no function is inferred. g436 and g20791 returned no match meeting the criterion (alnTM ≥ 0.5, E ≤ 0.05) in either database, g436 even after homolog-informed modelling. Gene structure and splice junctions support a conserved locus for the two-Trypsin-segment model g8114 (catalytic unit not established). A Boltz-2 thrombin pilot did not support target engagement, and a pre-registered nicotinic test was terminated as undecidable. The results yield a structure-informed shortlist for experimental follow-up.

Trisomy 21 Perturbs Oligodendrocyte Developmental States and Oligo–Neuron Communication in Human Forebrain Assembloids
record.abstract: Abstract Intellectual disability is a hallmark of Down syndrome (DS), caused by the triplication of human chromosome 21. Abnormal neuronal connectivity and impaired myelination are consistently observed in DS, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we used DS-derived isogenic induced pluripotent stem cell-derived forebrain assembloids (FAs) to investigate oligodendrocyte lineage cell (OLLC) development and neuron–glia interactions. Trisomic FAs exhibited an expansion of BCAS1+ pre-myelinating OLLCs, without a corresponding increase in myelin basic protein (MBP) expression. Transcriptomic analyses identified a euploid-enriched, trophic and maturation-supportive state (OLLC_2-TMS) and a trisomy-enriched synaptic interactions and differentiation state (OLLC_3-SID), lacking coordinated enrichment in myelination-promoting programs. Corresponding transcriptional signatures were identified in OLLCs from early postnatal human cortex. Increased excitatory neuronal contacts with pre-myelinating OLLCs accompanied ultrastructural myelin abnormalities in trisomic assembloids. Our findings suggest that trisomy redirects OLLC development toward a pre-myelinating state, uncoupling oligodendrocyte differentiation from productive myelination.

record.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
record.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM$+$0.08~eV, conclusively ruling out the previously proposed association with the B3 EPR center and its correlated deep donor level. Most significantly, we identify a metastable spin-1 triplet excited state separated from the singlet by $\sim$1.6~meV, consistent with the NL51 EPR signal. The $D_{2d}$ symmetry of the defect suppresses intersystem crossing and phosphorescence by first-order spin--orbit coupling, implying an exceptionally long spin--lattice relaxation time. Combined with a spectrally resolvable zero-field splitting and near-infrared emission, the triplet state of the I$_4$ complex constitutes a viable spin quantum memory intrinsic to silicon.

Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
record.abstract: Accurate calibration of tomographic redshift distributions, $N(z)$ is essential for cosmological analysis of weak lensing data. We investigate conditional normalizing flows (NFs) and compare their performance with random forest (RF) and quantile random forest (QRF) models. We consider DESI galaxy and quasar targets from DESI DR1 spectroscopic data and with the photometry from Legacy Surveys DR10. We train on 1.1 million sources and test on 2.0 million sources in a non-overlapping sky region ($0<z_{\rm spec}<4.5$). For point estimation, the NF achieves the lowest scatter and outlier fraction at $0<z_{\rm spec}<1.6$ and outperforms both baselines across all three metrics at $z_{\rm spec}>1.6$. By introducing distribution-level metrics like Wasserstein distance and JS divergence, we find that stacking NF posterior PDFs provides more accurate tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction than QRF, particularly at high redshifts. For $z_{\rm median}>2.5$, the NF achieves a smaller absolute mean-redshift bias ($0.060\pm0.031$ versus $0.318$) and higher probability overlap ($0.905\pm0.008$ versus $0.787$) than QRF. We apply redshift-dependent post-hoc PDF calibration derived from a held-out validation sample. After calibration, the absolute mean-redshift biases in four bins spanning $0.2<z_{\rm median}<1.0$ range from $0.0016$ to $0.0019$, with central values below referring benchmark $0.002(1+z)$. In the highest-redshift bin, calibration further reduces the bias to $0.016\pm0.011$. Our results demonstrate the potential of NF PDFs for tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction while highlighting challenges in transferring models across galaxy populations.

Teaching a Tree to Recover: Online Distillation of an LLM Supervisor with Counterfactual Replay
record.abstract: Autonomous mobile robots commonly pair a global planner with a local model predictive controller (MPC), but nonconvex obstacle avoidance and a limited horizon can make the robot freeze in complex layouts. Deciding whether to replan, wait, or call for help is a supervisory decision. Recent work queries a large language model (LLM) supervisor on every anomaly, which is slow and costly. We instead distill the LLM online into a decision tree. After each training episode, counterfactual replay labels recoveries as needed, unnecessary, or harmful. These labels retire unhelpful rules. In simulation, on 20 unseen layouts where the MPC alone freezes, the tree handles at least 18 correctly across all seeds, either by reaching the goal or by calling for help when no feasible path exists. The tree matches both an always-query LLM supervisor and expert-designed rules, while issuing no LLM queries at test time. Handwritten rules cannot anticipate the long tail of situations a physical robot will encounter. Online distillation is a promising remedy: the tree handles familiar cases, and the LLM is consulted only for new ones, whose validated recoveries become new rules. Language models can thus also serve as designers of supervisors rather than only as runtime supervisors.

record.title: Adaptive Sequential Surveillance of Infectious Diseases Under Limited Sampling Capacity
record.abstract: This paper develops a closed-loop adaptive sequential surveillance framework for infectious disease monitoring with limited surveillance resources. In this framework, we use a Bayesian spatio-temporal model to predict disease prevalence at each location, and propose several adaptive site-allocation strategies based on the posterior probabilities that the predictions exceed a predefined threshold. These strategies exploit high-risk locations while also exploring, by random or recency-based sampling or by incorporating the frontiers of emerging outbreaks. To address the unequal inclusion probabilities induced by adaptive sampling, we integrate inverse-probability weighting (IPW) into each model update. A simulation study showed that adaptive surveillance strategies improved outbreak detection relative to uniform sampling and fixed sentinel sampling. Frontier-based strategies improved detection and timeliness relative to risk-proportional allocation. When IPW was used to update the model, some proposed strategies yielded lower inferential bias compared with the standard unweighted update, particularly for strategies that allowed more flexible exploration. Credible-interval coverage varied by strategy. The results identify trade-offs between exploitation of known high-risk locations and exploration of potential outbreak frontiers.

record.title: NeuroEvolution of dynamic neural field architectures for Human–Robot joint action
record.abstract: Achieving adaptive Human–Robot Interaction (HRI) demands control architectures that generate behaviour through continuous sensorimotor dynamics. Dynamic Neural Fields (DNFs) offer a biologically inspired framework for modelling perception, memory, and action selection, yet designing functional neural-field controllers remains largely manual, limiting their scalability and broader adoption in robotic systems. Here, we introduce an approach for the automated synthesis of the architecture and dynamics of DNF controllers capable of generating normative joint-action behaviours. It builds on NEAT-DNFs, an extension of NeuroEvolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT) to neural-field architectures. From a perceptual–motor interface and a specification of the desired behaviour, the approach evolves both intrinsic field dynamics and architectural topology through mutation, crossover, and speciation. We evaluate it in a collaborative packaging task designed to isolate three basic coordination behaviours (complementary action selection, cooperative assistance, and action inhibition) and whose minimal controller can be derived analytically, providing a ground-truth reference for assessing evolved solutions. Across 100 independent runs, the approach discovered viable controllers in 97 cases. Ablation results show that structural growth, minimal initialisation, speciation, and crossover each contribute to performance, with the removal of any one component reducing the success rate, slowing convergence, or producing larger structures. The evolved architectures were topologically minimal, with interpretable activation dynamics grounded in known Dynamic Field Theory (DFT) mechanisms. The highest-performing minimal controller was deployed directly to a physical robot without parameter retuning, generalising to object arrangements beyond those used during evolution. Evolution converged most often on the minimal architecture without any specification of intermediate structure, indicating that behavioural requirements can drive the emergence of the internal processing structure the task requires. These findings demonstrate that functional DNF architectures for joint action can be evolved rather than hand-designed, shifting the designer’s contribution from specifying mechanism to specifying behaviour.

Multi-output LSTM soft sensors for industrial anaerobic co-digestion using LSTM-beta-VAE generative data augmentation
record.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) requires close monitoring of key process variables, including pH, the ratio of volatile organic acids to alkaline buffer capacity and biogas production, to maintain biological stability and prevent process failure. While mechanistic frameworks such as the Anaerobic Digestion Model No. 1 are highly parameterised, computationally expensive, and difficult to calibrate for real-time applications, data-driven Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks offer a potentially more adaptable alternative. However, current data-driven approaches in AD are predominantly limited to single-output architectures that focus solely on production yields, as opposed to simultaneous prediction of vital stability indicators. Furthermore, industrial AD datasets are typically sparse and skewed toward steady-state operations. Baseline evaluations demonstrated this scarcity prevents standard algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost) and unaugmented LSTMs from recognising the transition to unstable operations, resulting in poor estimation of stability indicators. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a novel generative data augmentation framework using an LSTM-beta-Variational Autoencoder coupled with a multi-output LSTM (MO-LSTM) soft sensor. By synthesising physically valid sequences of these transitions to unstable operations from one year of full-scale plant data, the method safely populates sparse regions of the feature space. Trained on this augmented dataset, the MO-LSTM achieved robust simultaneous estimation across all targets. This approach mitigates data sparsity, providing a basis for hybrid mechanistic-data-driven modelling and early-warning soft sensors in industrial bioprocesses.

record.title: Enabling Dynamic Resource Scaling in Quantum Circuit Simulations
record.abstract: Studies of quantum algorithms often simulate se- quences of circuits whose number of qubits changes from one circuit to the next, such as instances of increasing size of the same problem. Since each additional qubit doubles the state- vector, every circuit needs a different number of nodes, which a fixed allocation on a shared High-Performance Computing (HPC) system cannot provide: a job sized for the largest circuit leaves most of its nodes idle, and one job per circuit adds scheduler interactions and queue waits. We make the QuEST state-vector simulator malleable with the Dynamic Management of Resources (DMR) framework, so that a single job resizes between circuits. Because no state-vector exists between circuits, reconfigurations require no data redistribution and no changes to the simulation kernels, and a checkpoint holding the index of the next circuit is enough to resume. A right-sizing policy derives the number of nodes from the number of qubits, and the circuit_executor API hides reconfigurations from the user. We evaluate the reconfiguration overhead on MareNostrum 5 and show that a single job can run a batch of circuits of different sizes, adapting its allocation to each of them with negligible overhead.

record.title: High Burden of Shigellosis Among Hospitalized Children under five in Ndola, Zambia: Evidence from molecular-based surveillance
record.abstract: Abstract Background Shigella spp. is a leading cause of moderate-to-severe diarrhea and diarrheal mortality in children under five (CU5), globally. Traditional culture-based techniques consistently underestimates its prevalence, particularly in high-burden regions of sub-Saharan Africa. We aimed to generate population-relevant estimates of shigellosis among hospitalized children under five (CU5) in Ndola, Zambia, using a sensitive molecular diagnostic approach. Methods A prospective, hospital-based surveillance study was conducted at Arthur Davison Children’s Hospital (ADCH) from May 2020 to November 2021. All CU5 admitted with acute diarrhea (≥2 watery stools/day) were eligible. From enrolled children, sociodemographic and clinical data were collected, and stool samples were obtained where possible. Primary detection of Shigella spp./enteroinvasive E. coli (EIEC) was performed using loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) targeting the conserved ipaH gene. Operational shigellosis case-definition: A child with diarrhea (2 or more watery stools/day) and a stool sample positive for the ipaH gene by LAMP. Prevalence of shigellosis was calculated among children with LAMP-tested samples and weighted to account for all admissions. The incidence of hospitalization was estimated using the district CU5 population denominators. Results Among 1,685 enrolled children, 950 provided stool samples. LAMP detected ipaH in 186 samples (19.6%;95% CI: 17.1–22.5). The weighted prevalence among all admissions was 19.5% (95% CI: 17.5–21.5) corresponding to 329 cases. The incidence of shigellosis hospitalization was 2.4 (95% CI: 2.2–2.7) per 1,000 person-years. The burden exhibited a distinct age distribution, peaking in children aged 12–23 months, preceded by an evident rise in the number of cases between 6 and 12 months of age. Shigellosis was associated with bloody diarrhea, increased stool frequency, and fever. Pre-admission antibiotic or other medication use was reported in 33% of cases. Conclusions Shigellosis accounts for a substantial proportion of severe diarrhea requiring hospitalization in Ndola, Zambia. Findings support improved diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and prioritization of Shigella vaccines.

record.title: LAMP: LLM-Driven Analog Placement through Adaptive Tool Composition
record.abstract: Analog placement requires circuit-specific trade-offs among area, matching, routability, and electrical performance. Balancing these trade-offs through predefined objectives and fixed placement flows remains difficult. In this paper, we propose an analog placement framework in which a large language model (LLM) acts as a layout engineer through composable placement components. These components support constraint management, placement and legalization, and lightweight evaluation of routability and electrical performance. Using multimodal checkpoints of the initial and evolving design, the LLM selects and combines components to construct and revise its own placement flow. It also adapts the placement hierarchy by reopening modules or partitioning and regrouping devices, allowing local layouts to respond to global design needs. An experience skill provides reusable design knowledge to guide these decisions. Evaluation on two SMIC 180 nm circuits shows that the framework reduces placement area and improves most measured post-layout performance metrics.

Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
record.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) edge pipelines routinely lose contiguous blocks of multi-sensor data to network dropouts and hardware faults. The standard remedy is a disjointed "impute-then-detect" pipeline whose imputer is trained only for Mean Squared Error (MSE). Such an imputer fills a missing block with the most probable normal pattern: a partially observed anomaly is smoothed back toward normality, and boundary artifacts on normal data raise false alarms. We call this imputation bias and propose the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR), a conditional diffusion refiner trained against the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector. Because back-propagating through the sampling trajectory is intractable, the task-aware terms act on the one-step clean-window estimate that the noise prediction already yields, so training costs no more than plain diffusion training. Under strict Point-to-Point evaluation over five seeds with paired significance tests, TADR raises F1 by $0.338$ over the unrefined detector on SMD ($p = 0.0015$), and the anomaly enhancement objective alone contributes $0.463$ in ablation. We also characterise when the method helps: the gain tracks the continuous, mutually redundant channels available and the anomaly evidence the outage removes, and it is absent on telemetry datasets dominated by one-hot command channels and on PSM. At ten sampling steps TADR runs in $41.4$ ms per window on a single CPU core, sustaining about $24$ concurrent 1 Hz streams from a $4.03$ MB model. Code and per-seed results are available at https://github.com/int-park422/TADR.

record.title: Federated Agentic AI for Interference-Aware Adaptive Spectrum Coordination
record.abstract: Emerging intelligent wireless networks increasingly rely on autonomous AI agents to adapt spectrum usage to dynamic and heterogeneous operating conditions. However, collective learning is challenging when agents experience different local interference environments and cannot exchange raw observations due to communication-overhead and privacy constraints. We propose Federated Agentic Spectrum Coordination with Interference Awareness (FASCIA), a federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for adaptive spectrum coordination. In FASCIA, each network manager acts as an autonomous AI agent that perceives its local interference environment, accumulates experience in a persistent local memory, and learns an adaptive spectrum coordination policy through local interactions. Coordination among agents is achieved through periodic federated aggregation of locally trained models, without exchanging raw sensing data or experience. Since spectrum decisions made by one agent alter the environments observed by others, local learning is inherently heterogeneous and coupled. FASCIA employs proximal regularization to mitigate the resulting model drift and explicitly accounts for inter-carrier interference arising from partially overlapping channels. FASCIA is the first federated agentic AI framework to address this challenging interference-coupled spectrum coordination setting. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FASCIA achieves performance close to the centralized benchmark while avoiding raw-experience exchange and maintaining effectiveness across heterogeneous network configurations.

record.title: Exploring the Potential of Symbolic Regression in Precision Livestock Farming
record.abstract: The ability to predict farrowing time in pigs is crucial for optimal farm management and ensuring piglet survival. This study investigates the potential of explainable artificial intelligence for precision livestock farming, focusing on acceleration sensor data from sows around the time of farrowing. Accurately predicting farrowing allows farmers to balance both, piglet safety by avoiding piglet crushing events and the mother sow's welfare, by avoiding early crating. Traditional machine learning models often lack interpretability (``closed-box'' problem). Explainable artificial intelligence offers a solution by revealing the decision-making processes within the models. This work is split into two stages. First the detection of nest building behaviour and second the prediction of the remaining time to farrowing. The nest building detection was possible for 166 out of 180 sows and successful within 48 hours before farrowing for 149 sows. The nest building detection is purely based on the change of a sow's activity level and uses no machine learning techniques. Further, this study utilizes symbolic regression, an open-box modelling technique that generates interpretable mathematical formulas, to predict the remaining time until the onset of farrowing. The results are compared with closed-box models, like support vector regression and artificial neural networks, for both explainability and performance. Notably, symbolic regression achieved a mean absolute error of 9.28 hours for the time-to-farrowing prediction, outperforming the closed-box models in terms of performance and interpretability. This research demonstrates that explainable artificial intelligence, specifically symbolic regression, can offer both interpretable results and competitive performance in precision livestock farming.

record.title: Single-cell foundation models transfer across deep evolutionary distances
record.abstract: Abstract Single-cell foundation models are trained mostly on human and other vertebrate cells, yet are proposed as general-purpose models. Whether they transfer far beyond their training species is unknown. We evaluated zero-shot embeddings from Geneformer, scGPT and UCE against PCA and scVI in developmental atlases of Dictyostelium discoideum and Caenorhabditis elegans , separated from humans by 1.2 billion and 600 million years. Without retraining, the models recovered developmental order and preserved organism-specific cell identities. UCE encodes genes by protein sequence and could use 97% of measured genes, whereas Geneformer and scGPT, after ortholog mapping, used under one-fifth. UCE performed most consistently, often exceeding species-native baselines. Restricted to ortholog-mappable genes, it still scored above vocabulary-based models on five of six annotation tasks, some narrowly. Foundation models can thus yield informative cell embeddings across more than a billion years of evolution, and protein-sequence gene representations make these embeddings more complete and often more accurate.

record.title: Full Scan Enhanced Dynamic Range MS Improves Metabolite Coverage and Cancer Cell Line Discrimination in Untargeted Metabolomics
record.abstract: Abstract Metabolite detection with mass spectrometry (MS) in untargeted metabolomics is limited by the wide concentration range of metabolites, where high-abundance ions can restrict the detection of low-abundance features. Full Scan enhanced Dynamic Range (eDR) MS addresses this limitation by partitioning the MS1 mass range into multiple subscans and mass windows, reducing ion competition during accumulation. Here, we systematically evaluated different eDR acquisition strategies for untargeted metabolomics. Across four hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines, Full Scan eDR MS increased detectable compounds up to ∼3.5-fold compared with Full Scan MS and improved signal-to-noise ratios of low-abundance compounds. Among equidistant configurations, 12 windows yielded the highest compound count, while custom window distributions enabled targeted enhancement of selected mass regions. In particular, allocating narrower windows to the low-m/z region selectively increased the detection of low-mass compounds. Increased MS1 coverage also translated into deeper MS2 coverage and increased metabolite identifications. This expanded coverage included cancer-relevant metabolites and improved the detection of metabolic differences between cancer cell lines. Overall, Full Scan eDR MS provides a flexible strategy to increase analytical depth in untargeted metabolomics while maintaining data quality. Customization of window size and distribution enables targeted expansion of the dynamic range within predefined mass regions, allowing MS acquisition to be tailored to sample composition and metabolites of interest.

record.title: Searching for axion-like particles with space-based optical lattice clock networks
record.abstract: Axion like particles (ALPs) are particularly well motivated candidates for dark matter, and physics beyond the Standard Model more generally. However, direct detection remains extremely challenging due to the weakness of their interactions. In this work, we propose to employ space-based optical lattice clock networks (SOLCN), originally targeted to probe the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB), to detect axion dark matter through cosmic birefringence via minor modifications to their laser links. Searching for cross-correlated signals then provides significant sensitivity to low mass ALPs as a result of their large correlation lengths. In this work we focus on ALPs in the mass range $10^{-18.55}\text{eV}-10^{-14}\text{eV}$, For ALPs mass region $10^{-18}-10^{-14}\text{eV}$, finding that we can probe down to $g_{aγ}\geq 10^{-12}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}$. Moreover, we find that the SOLCN sensitivity to the ALP-photon coupling depends crucially on the frequency of the network link. With an $8$ GHz frequency link, we then have the potential to reach $g_{aγ}\geq10^{-16}\,\text{GeV}^{-1}$ in this region.

record.title: Grammar Control for Language Learning with Sequential Monte Carlo and Small Language Models
record.abstract: Second language learners benefit from exposure to level-appropriate grammar in interactive language use. While prompted frontier language models can usually produce target grammar structures, less resource-intensive models that can be run on device often fail in this task. We use sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to steer dialogue turn generation in small lan- language models toward target grammar constructions from an expert-developed pedagogical resource. With a minimal set of hand-coded potential functions, SMC achieves near-perfect coverage of target grammar, enabling small models to outperform state-of-the-art results from models 140 times larger. We also use code synthesis with frontier models to generate new potentials, showing that our method scales to hundreds of target grammar skills with no need for additional training or supervised data.

record.title: ChAI-Net learns a regulatory code for chromatin co-accessibility
Edge intelligence for distributed acoustic sensing with ultracompact neural networks
record.abstract: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) transforms optical fibres into dense arrays of vibration sensors for continuous, long-range monitoring with high spatial resolution. Yet converting these large-scale measurements into actionable information with compact models that retain task performance remains challenging. Existing artificial-intelligence approaches are typically optimized for specific sensing environments and tasks, but their computational requirements can hinder deployment in compact, power-constrained field systems. Here, we introduce DAS-NanoNet, a framework that automatically constructs lightweight neural networks for different DAS scenarios and tasks, together with OmniDAS, an open benchmark spanning six representative environments. Using lightweight temporal operators tailored to DAS signals, an adaptive neural architecture search strategy derives a compact network for each scenario-task pairing. Across classification, localization, compression, and denoising tasks in diverse DAS applications, DAS-NanoNet consistently yields highly compact architectures. On a six-class dataset, it achieves 99.68% accuracy with only 1,391 trainable parameters, while delivering comparable or better performance with up to 18,098-fold fewer parameters than previously reported high-accuracy networks. Its compact architecture further enables edge deployment, achieving sub 9 $μ$s inference latency on the deployed hardware platform across different DAS applications. DAS-NanoNet provides a route towards edge intelligence for compact, low-power and real-time DAS systems through ultracompact networks tailored to individual sensing scenarios and tasks.

record.title: Digital pathological classification of peripheral neuroblastic tumors across multi-continent cohorts
Electrically controlled heat assisted magnetic manipulation in intercalated 2D magnets
record.abstract: Abstract The ever-increasing demand for fast, reliable, and energy-efficient information storage continues to push magnetic memory technologies toward their fundamental limits. Conventional scaling strategies, which rely on reducing bit size, inevitably run into the “magnetic recording trilemma,” where signal-to-noise ratio, thermal stability, and writability cannot all be optimized simultaneously. Heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) has emerged as the leading solution, enabling high-density storage by transiently heating the medium during the write cycle. However, the reliance on laser optics and plasmonic transducers restricts HAMR primarily to hard-disk drives, limiting its integration with on-chip or embedded architectures. Here, we demonstrate an electronic variant of HAMR in which Joule heating from low-current density current pulses facilitates data writing, while the anomalous Hall effect provides electronic readout. Employing intercalated 2D magnet Ni 1/4 TaSe 2 , we show direct evidence that current pulses heat the material above its Curie temperature, during which a small magnetic field of 2 mT(100 times smaller than the coercive field) enables efficient data writing. The all-electronic approach combined with the 2D magnetic medium creates timely opportunities to revisit the energy-assisted magnetization recording, enabling new schemes that combine fundamental novelty with technological impact.

BiHashFormer: Hash-Driven Dual-Branch Transformer for Efficient Object Detection in HRW Shots
record.abstract: Recent advances in gigapixel-level imaging have brought High-Resolution Wide shots to the forefront of research. However, these images present significant challenges: extreme sparsity of foreground, gigapixel-level resolutions and interleaving of foreground and background. This causes traditional detectors and attention mechanisms to be hindered by background, resulting in inefficiency and inaccuracy. To tackle this problem, we propose BiHashFormer, a dual sparsified branch transformer built on hashing. RoI Selector will predict the foreground proportion for top-k selecting target-containing windows. The compression branch processes windows selected and refines attention into HashAttention by discarding half of the key-value pairs, reducing cost and improving efficiency. The compensation branch uses HashMiner to perform low-cost hash searches in the remaining regions, recovering features of missed objects. Experiments confirm that the selection relationship in HashAttention is one-way and reveal the preference of different queries for keys. In experiments on the gigapixel benchmark PANDA, BiHashFormer reduces 37.5% backbone FLOPs while improving AP50 to 81.0%. Moreover, this parallel dual-branch structure allows the model to avoid inference delays caused by inter-branch dependencies, while achieving much greater stability than single-branch models, specially with low rates of RoI selection.

record.title: A vessel trajectory prediction method integrating Conditional Variational Autoencoder with TrAISformer
record.abstract: Predicting vessel trajectories in complex maritime routes is challenging because several future paths may be plausible and autoregressive errors accumulate over long horizons. We propose CVAE-TrAISformer, an extension of TrAISformer inspired by conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) that augments its stochastic categorical predictor with context-conditioned latent features. A latent branch aggregates the available autoregressive context, samples latent variables through reparameterization, and fuses them with Automatic Identification System (AIS) embeddings before the Transformer; training uses categorical prediction losses and annealed Kullback-Leibler regularization. On the Danish Maritime Authority AIS benchmark, oracle best-of -16 mean prediction errors at 1, 2, and 3 h decrease from 0.48, 0.94, and 1.64 nautical miles for TrAISformer to 0.39, 0.77, and 1.30 nautical miles, respectively, with 0.96% more parameters. A separate paired ten-run fixed-latent evaluation identifies a significant reduction in 3-h endpoint error for complex trajectories (Holm-adjusted p = 0.023). Candidate-set analyses show lower displacement errors across evaluated set sizes but no increased spatial dispersion or consistent branch-coverage advantage. Kinematic diagnostics show more frequent large course-over-ground changes. These findings support improved oracle-evaluated long-horizon accuracy while identifying limits of latent conditioning.

record.title: Coherent dynamics of individual excitons in a quantum dot embedded in a nanopost
record.abstract: We measured coherent ultrafast dynamics of exciton complexes in a single strongly-confined InAs quantum dot embedded in a GaAs nanopost. Such a photonic structure combines a wave guiding with a cavity effect and assures an enhanced light-matter coupling over a broad spectral range of 30 nm. Coherence properties of an exciton-biexciton system hosted by a quantum dot are assessed with four-wave mixing microscopy. Our results show that this broad-band photonic structure is an excellent asset to probe coherent couplings in a small set of solid state quantum systems and to investigate the coherence dynamics within the level structure of their excited states.

record.title: ElasticFormer: Detecting Objects in HRW Shots via Elastic Computing Vision Transformer
record.publication: Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), pp. 32735-32744, 2026
record.abstract: Recent advances in gigapixel-level imaging have brought High-Resolution Wide shots to the forefront of research. However, these images present significant challenges: extreme sparsity of foreground, gigapixel-level resolutions and diverse target counts. This makes traditional close-up detectors inaccurate and slow as they are overwhelmed by the background. Although previous research has explored sparse backbones, their fixed sparsity patterns lack the adaptability required to handle diverse target numbers. To address this, we introduce ElasticFormer, a sparse backbone that dynamically allocates computational resources based on foreground proportion. After scoring windows based on variance, proposed ElasticSelector module will predict the foreground proportion for top-k selection. The mechanism guides the model to select target-containing windows, scaling resources in areas where objects are clustered. We introduce a novel loss function combined with the 3-phase training strategy for ElasticSelector, allowing it to function properly when bounding box annotations are missing. A WSOD study is carried on PASCAL VOC 2007 to evaluate its extensibility. Further, ElasticNet is created to verify its backbone-agnostic nature. In experiments on the PANDA gigapixel benchmark, ElasticFormer reduces backbone FLOPs by 80% while achieving a significant improvement in AP50 when compared to fixed-ratio sparse methods.
